Visit note | 2025-04-21 03:00 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Rashid Chowdhury, 54, male. Mr. Chowdhury states he feels a racing heart and dislikes the heat. He noticed this when his clothes became loose during a stay in Motijheel. He works as a homemaker and has no notable comorbidities. He denies chest pain or tremor. On examination: pulse 113 bpm, BP 117/85 mmHg, weight 91 kg. Thyroid is diffusely enlarged. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee and to rest when the heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-04-21 04:00 PM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Sajjad Sikder, 59, male. Mr. Sikder reports his symptoms are worse with dust, alongside a runny nose. He mentions these troubles have been worse since keeping a cat at home in Banani. He is a police constable and has no chronic illnesses. He denies shortness of breath. On examination: about 12 sneezing fits a day, BP 114/80 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 53 kg. Nasal mucosa is pale and boggy. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-04-21 04:30 PM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Mitu Munshi, 63, female. Mrs. Munshi complains that her eyelids are stuck together in the morning and her eye is red. She states this started after a family member in Banani had red eyes. She works as a madrasa teacher and has no other medical conditions. She denies visual loss or severe pain. On examination: visual acuity 6/18 in the right eye, BP 127/75 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 71 kg. Conjunctiva is injected with purulent discharge. Assessment: Bacterial conjunctivitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to wash her hands often, not share towels, and stay away from work for two days. Follow-up in 1 week if not better.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 10:00 AM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Rafiq Islam, 67, male. Mr. Islam reports no symptoms, but high cholesterol was found on a routine test, and his father had a heart attack at 55. He noticed this after a relative's heart attack in Kamrangirchar prompted testing. He is a madrasa teacher and has no comorbidities. He denies chest discomfort or palpitations. On examination: LDL cholesterol 5.8 mmol/L, BP 115/76 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 62 kg. Heart sounds are normal. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 10:30 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Arif Siddique, 31, male. Mr. Siddique describes a fear of dying and sudden attacks of a racing heart. He notes his first attack happened at a busy market in Bogura. He works as a cricket coach and has no known comorbidity. He denies chronic sadness or suicidal ideation. On examination: about 12 panic attacks in the last month, BP 129/86 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 89 kg. Mental status examination reveals anxious mood with autonomic arousal. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 11:00 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Marium Howlader, 27, female. Mrs. Howlader attends for review regarding her fear of dying and sudden attacks of a racing heart. She reports her first attack happened at a busy market in Shyamoli. She is a journalist with no other medical issues. She denies depressive symptoms. On examination: about 11 panic attacks in the last month, BP 127/76 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 62 kg. She was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 02:00 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Fatema Akter, 58, female. Mrs. Akter comes back for a review of a blocked ear after a cold, ear pain, and mild fever. She notes this started after swimming in a pond in Farmgate. She works as a madrasa teacher and has no other illnesses. She denies dizziness. On examination: temperature 101.2°F, BP 122/81 mmHg, pulse 101 bpm, weight 93 kg. Otoscopy shows an inflamed, bulging tympanic membrane. Assessment: Acute otitis media. Visit note | 2025-04-22 02:00 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Hossain Rahman, 38, male. Mr. Rahman states he has swelling of the eyelid and a painful red lump at the edge of the eyelid. He mentions it appeared during a stressful week in Chattogram. He is a garment factory worker and has a history of Bronchial asthma. He denies visual impairment. On examination: lump about 3 mm on the right upper eyelid, BP 136/74 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 62 kg. Eye shows localized lid margin tenderness and swelling. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use a warm compress four times a day, not squeeze the lump, and avoid eye makeup. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 02:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Habiba Chowdhury, 25, female. Ms. Chowdhury returns for review, reporting poor sleep, low mood for over three weeks, and no interest in usual activities. She states this began after moving away from family to Tejgaon. She works as a textile engineer and has no physical comorbidity. She denies psychotic symptoms. On examination: PHQ-9 score 11, BP 116/75 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 57 kg. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 03:00 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Dilruba Khatun, 40, female. Mrs. Khatun attends for a follow-up visit regarding a racing heart and hating the heat. She noticed this when her clothes became loose during a stay in Cumilla. She works as a restaurant cook and has no other chronic diseases. She denies heat intolerance without palpitations. On examination: pulse 121 bpm, BP 126/75 mmHg, weight 56 kg. Tremors are present in outstretched hands. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. Visit note | 2025-04-22 03:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Uttam Dey, 68, male. Mr. Dey complains of a stiff shoulder for weeks, being unable to reach behind the back, and being unable to raise the arm. He states this began gradually after a long illness in Tangail. He works as a shopkeeper and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies recent shoulder trauma or dislocation. On examination: shoulder lifts only to 70 degrees, BP 135/73 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 85 kg. Range of active and passive movement is restricted. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 03:00 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Ziaur Patwary, 40, male. Mr. Patwary presents for his first visit complaining of a painful red lump at the edge of his left eyelid along with noticeable swelling of the eyelid itself. He reports that this troubling issue appeared after using old eye makeup in Tangail during a weekend visit. He works as a software developer and mentions a past medical history of Bronchial asthma, which is currently stable. He denies any visual changes, double vision, or discharge from the other eye. On examination, a prominent lump measuring about 7 mm is observed on the left upper eyelid, accompanied by localized erythema and tenderness. His vital signs show a blood pressure of 115/81 mmHg, a regular pulse of 75 bpm, and a body weight of 86 kg. The cornea is clear and visual acuity is unimpaired. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued today. He was strongly advised to use a warm compress four times a day, strictly avoid squeezing or trying to pop the lump, and refrain from wearing any eye makeup until fully healed. Follow-up is scheduled in 1 week to check on the resolution of the stye.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 03:30 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Sabina Pramanik, 61, female. Mrs. Pramanik comes in for a review complaining of pain behind her eyes, severe aching in her bones and muscles, and a faint rash on her arms. She mentions this started after a week of stagnant rainwater around the house in Rajshahi. She is an NGO field officer with no other chronic illnesses. She denies bleeding manifestations. On examination: platelet count 91000 per microlitre, temperature 102.9°F, BP 118/79 mmHg, pulse 105 bpm, weight 83 kg. Skin shows a mild flushing rash. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 04:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Hafsa Miah, 48, female. Mrs. Miah returns for a review, stating she needs to lie in a dark room and has a throbbing headache on one side. She mentions her attacks are triggered by skipping meals while travelling in Jatrabari. She works as a mobile phone repair technician and has no comorbidity. She denies focal neurological deficits. On examination: about 10 headache days a month, BP 130/81 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 49 kg. Neurological examination is unremarkable. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.

Visit note | 2025-04-22 04:30 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Mahmuda Siddique, 37, female. Mrs. Siddique complains of a lower belly ache and burning when passing urine. She notes this started after a trip to Old Dhaka. She works as a textile engineer and has no comorbidities. She denies vaginal discharge or loin pain. On examination: temperature 99.0°F, BP 135/84 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 92 kg. Suprapubic tenderness is present. Assessment: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least two litres of water daily and not hold urine for long. Follow-up in 1 week if symptoms continue.

Visit note | 2025-04-23 09:00 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Shapla Khatun, 73, female. She was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-04-23 10:30 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Champa Howlader, 62, female. Visit note | 2025-04-23 10:30 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Mahbub Kabir, 18, male. Visit note | 2025-04-23 10:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Ratan Datta, 19, male. Visit note | 2025-04-23 12:00 PM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Rokeya Faruque, 28, female.
